senses: Having a heel (of a specified type).
Tending to crouch; hunched over.
examples: They run very low, all crouchy, and so do panthers, which was a surprise to me.
So then all of sudden he starts doing that crouchy thing, you know, when he looks like a lion on the hunt.

senses: Something that lasts or takes a specified number of minutes.
A level staff or graduated rod used by surveyors to measure differences in level, or to measure horizontal distances by sighting the stadia hairs (graduations) through a telescope.
Referring to bacterial infections that make pus.
A net designed to keep hair up and out of the way, e.g. while cooking.
ety: From hair + net. Compare Dutch haarnetje, German Haarnetz, Danish hårnet, Swedish hårnät.

senses: A strong-jawed North Atlantic fish of wolffish family Anarhichadidae, Anarhichas lupus.
ety: From Middle English sēwolf, from Old English *sǣwulf, equivalent to sea + wolf.

senses: A form of shish kebab, originally made of marinated lamb meat.
ety: Borrowed from Russian шашлы́к (šašlýk), from Crimean Tatar şışlıq / шишлик (şişlik, “something to be cooked on a skewer”), ultimately from Turkic; compare Turkish şaşlık/ şişlik. Doublet of chislic.
examples: Men entered the room bearing skewers of tikas—kebabs or shashliki, we would call them—spitted chunks of lamb that had been roasted with onions and other seasoning.

Everyone went to the Pump Room where the children would be entertained by the Nubian Slaves with flaming skewers of shashlik, while their parents talked to Irving Kupcinet, the Eiffel Tower of Chicago columnists.

They swam and fished by day, they drank wine and grilled shashliki in the evenings, and sometimes they drove into Yalta to enjoy the night-life, but throughout it all Minka remained detached, like a convalescent.

senses: An act of blinking one's eyelids one time.
A moment (a very short period of time).
ety: From eye + blink. Cognate with Afrikaans oomblik, Dutch ogenblik, German Augenblick, German Low German Ogenblick.

senses: The wood of the hazel.
A traditional Puerto Rican alcoholic eggnog made with coconut.
A station wagon shaped like a small bus.
examples: Well, we shot the line and we went for broke With a thousand screamin' trucks An' eleven long-haired Friends a' Jesus In a chartreuse microbus.

senses: A very short summary of a script or screenplay.
ety: First attested in 1613 as logge-line. A compound of log + line.

senses: One who bares or exposes something.
examples: What on earth do they think they are doing, this legion of barers of poets' souls: apart, of course, from making a few bob for, and enhancing the reputations of, their publishers and themselves?

senses: A jot or tittle; the smallest amount.
ety: Borrowed from Hindustani حَبَّہ (habba) / हब्बा (habbā), from Classical Persian حبه (habba), from Arabic حَبَّة (ḥabba).
examples: The camp Banyans, to make their purchases of him, pay the assize your Highness may fix, and not a hubba shall be taken without payment being made.

senses: A tendency to remain at, or move towards the centre.
A man who is a member of a committee
A man who is a local leader of a political party
(US) A pie, having pastry sides and bottom and (usually also) top, and filled with savory fillings, such as meat, root vegetables, or (often) both.
Especially, such a pie that is small, that has crust made entirely of flaky pastry, and that is baked in its own pie tin, usually for one person (single-serve).
A dish of meat and vegetable stew with dumplings.
A very tiny amount.
ety: From French micron, from Ancient Greek μικρόν (mikrón), neuter of μικρός (mikrós, “small”).

senses: The state of being practicable; feasibility
Suitable or available for inclusion.
A female vampire.
examples: Here, the vampiress personifies righteous indignation, a one-woman lynch mob.

senses: A traditional bread eaten by Ashkenazi Jews, usually braided for the Sabbath and round for a yom tov.
The commandment to separate a portion of bread or bread dough for the cohanim (Numbers 15:17–21); in contemporary practice, the portion is burned until inedible.
The portion separated in fulfillment of the above.
ety: From Hebrew חַלָּה (ḥallá, “loaf”), influenced by Yiddish חלה (khale).

senses: Having spots; spotted.
Occurring in non-contiguous positions or locations.
Of inconsistent quality.
Inconsistent: not reliably good, sometimes bad.
ety: From Middle English spotty, equivalent to spot + -y.
examples: Mobile phone reception in this area tends to be rather spotty.
Many of the buyers had a spotty credit history.
Many of the low-cost accessories (cords, chargers, etc) sold in the dollar store had spotty quality.

senses: A genre of Angolan popular music derived from the traditional semba dance.
The residence of the minister of a parish.
A type of sugar made from the extract of sugar cane
examples: Turbinado is usually made by squeezing the juice out of crushed sugar cane, then spinning what's left after evaporation through a huge centrifuge.

senses: The base of a sword or knife blade where it joins the tang.
The blunt area of a sword just above the hilt, used for grip and maneuverability.
The comparable portion of a knife.
ety: Borrowed from Italian ricasso. Further etymology unknown.

senses: A dish of black beans and white riced cooked together; congri.
ety: From its Spanish name, Spanish moros y cristianos (literally “Moors and Christians”), in reference to the colors of the two ingredients.
examples: This is good served with black bean soup and rice or moros or congri.

senses: Excellent, when referring to eggs or Easter.
examples: Food trends specialist Phil Lempert offered several "eggcellent" ideas for marketing eggs during his recent remarks to the United Egg Producers.
She Crabs laden with egg make very eggcellent soup.

senses: In Portugal and Brazil, a million reis.
ety: Borrowed from Portuguese conto. Doublet of computus.

senses: Having a specified type of complexion.
That which sates.
Disgusted; repulsed; creeped out.
ety: Formed of skeeve + -ed, from Italian schifo (“disgust, nausea”), schifare (“to disgust, to loathe”), and schifoso (“disgusting, loathsome”).
examples: It took him days to get over how skeeved he was.
But like other "red flag" finds — undies, lingerie, bikini bottoms — you might be a little too skeeved to actually let one touch your naked body.
We're so embarrassed about our bodies, so "skeeved" about our periods and smells and hair, we can't even bring ourselves to touch ourselves.

senses: An expert or specialist in embryology
Synonym of calamander.
Synonym of Chinese violet.
ety: From the Coromandel Coast in India, a source of this wood.
examples: Rhoda took their battered hats, led the women upstairs for hairpins, and presently fed them all with tea-cakes, poached eggs, anchovy toast, and drinks from a coromandel-wood liqueur case.

senses: A specialist in odontology.
A device used to thread needles.
A device used to machine a screw thread.
An ornament consisting of a single rapid alternation between a given pitch and another pitch either a whole step or half step immediately above or below it.
ety: From Italian mordente. Doublet of mordant.

senses: omnium-gatherum
examples: A gatherum of birds which cannot well be accommodated elsewhere in separate collections.
